newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans tumble on poor exports, Brazil rains.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans tumble on poor exports, Brazil rains.

text.p: Disappointing USDA weekly export sales and rain in Brazil's soybean growing regions sent soybean futures tumbliag on Thursday, traders said.
"There was more rain and the exports weren't very good," said Vic Lespinasse of Dean Witter. "All that's weighing on beans and beans are pulling everything else down."
USDA Thursday pegged weekly net export sales at 348,700 tonnes, near the bottom of trade expectations for 300,000 to 500,000 tonnes.
Overnight rains in Brazil's Rio Grande do Sul doused fears of drought-related crop losses, traders said.
But some Brazilian producers noted monthly rainfall was at 40 mm, below with the 15-year monthly average of 150 mm.
On the day, Continental Grain sold three million bushels March and E.D. and F. Man International, Merrill Lynch Futures, Rosenthal Collins and Dean Witter each sold 1.5 million March, traders said.
In options trade, Goldenberg-Hehmeyer bought 400 March $7.25 puts at 4-3/8 to 5 cents per bushel. Smith Barney sold 500 May $8.00 calls at 8 to 8-1/4, traders said.
Soybeans ended 8-3/4 to six cents per bushel lower with March off 8-1/2 at $7.41-1/2 a bushel.
